problem: It says a yes/no condition has one valid class (true) and one invalid class (false). When the specification allows either answer, both true and false are valid classes; calling false invalid is wrong and a student will repeat it in the exam.
fix: A yes/no input where both answers are allowed gives two valid classes, true and false. False is an invalid class only when the rule requires yes (for example, a terms-and-conditions checkbox that must be ticked).

problem: "Write one test case per class ... so the number of test cases equals the number of classes" is only true for a single input item. With several input items, one test case usually carries a valid representative from each input at once, so the count is not simply the number of classes.
fix: For a single input item, one test case per class, so the count equals the number of classes. With several input items, cover all valid classes of one input in the same case where possible, and use one case per invalid class; the count is the largest number of valid classes for any one input plus the total number of invalid classes.

problem: "A list of n items: classes for 0 items, 1 to max items, and more than max" mixes n and an undefined "max", so the symbol is not tied to the rule.
fix: A list that accepts up to n items gives three classes: 0 items, 1 to n items, and more than n items.

problem: The fare check appears from nowhere: the specification in the example mentions only age and the senior discount, and a railway fare depends on many things besides age, so the step does not follow from the rules read in step 1.
fix: State the expected output that the specification does fix, for example: the form accepts or rejects the age and shows the senior discount message for ages 60 to 120; each of the nine cases checks that message.
